adaptation_principles: Use the source module as structural support, not as campaign truth.
Keep C1S4 observed recap and source module facts separate.
Treat user modifications as adaptation notes, not automatic source facts.
Prefer source elements as prep candidates; promote only when used or confirmed.
Answer with authority labels: source-supported, adaptation-inferred, observed-canon, creative.

mappings.notes: Hempholm remains the hemp-associated village crisis site, but regional/Faerun context should be replaced by Elderwyld/Longmont context.
Core visible threat retained: enormous, dangerous, magical/metallic tree. Table version may change exact stats, reach, growth timing, and presentation.
Boy/witness role retained. Campaign framing can emphasize sadness, fear, being beaten, or guilt rather than copying source dialogue.
Irate father/survival-pressure role retained; campaign version may compress or rename Mark Jove to Jove.
The PDF includes generic/formal hooks and merchant rumor structures; the campaign adaptation uses Torvak Hempdealer as the memorable road hook NPC.
Source hemp economy supports Torvak's role and Hempholm's identity, but exact trade/geography should be adapted.
Saladin is useful optional source material but should not appear as campaign canon unless intentionally introduced.
Morwin/store can provide village texture if needed, but is not automatically part of observed C1S4 canon.
Narfi can provide healer/social support if the adapted session needs a village NPC, but should not be assumed present.
The source uses the Shacks for lodging and celebration. The campaign can adapt this into any town revelry/gathering location.

mappings.campaign_element: precious metal leaves / metallic tree remains
mappings.notes: Precious metal remains are a strong retained loot/material hook; exact value and crafting use may differ.

mappings.source_element: tree/root material as valuable crafting material
mappings.notes: The observed/adapted table can turn source treasure/materials into PC-specific crafting interactions.
Core second-wave threat retained: root/caretaker creatures emerge after the visible tree is destroyed. Campaign language can present them as beetles.
False-victory celebration retained; campaign can add social friction, PC-specific choices, or ugly local behavior.
Racist/socially ugly townsperson is campaign-specific texture; do not derive from PDF unless explicitly present in adaptation notes.
The PDF's descent can support future-session prep after the beetle eruption, but should be optional until campaign play confirms direction.
The child/helix reveal is potent source material but not automatically part of Longmont canon.
The mages' guild cleanup hook should be transformed or omitted unless it fits Elderwyld campaign institutions.

prior_only.expected_behavior: Infer broad next-session shape only; do not name Hempholm-specific source facts.

prior_plus_support.expected_behavior: Use Hempholm/source-module facts as planning support while preserving authority labels.

allowed: C1S4 oracle targets/recap according to grader policy
forbidden: planner-visible use of C1S4 during prep generation
oracle_grading.expected_behavior: Compare generated prep against observed C1S4 without leaking oracle to planner.
